verses.sanskrit: बृहदश्व उवाच। प्रशान्ते तु पुरे हृष्टे संप्रवृत्ते महोत्सवे। महत्या सेनया राजा दमयन्तीमुपानयत्॥१॥
verses.english: Brihadashva said: When the great festivities began in the city which was full of joy, the king with a large army brought Damayanti (back to his capital).

verses.sanskrit: दमयन्तीमपि पिता सत्कृत्य परवीरहा। प्रास्थापयदमेयात्मा भीमो भीमपराक्रमः॥२॥
verses.english: Her father, that slayer of hostile heroes Bhima of great prowess and of high soul, also having honoured her duly, sent Damayanti (tc her husband's palace).

verses.sanskrit: आगतायां तु वैदर्भ्यां सपुत्रायां नलो नृपः। वर्तयामास मुदितो देवराडिव नन्दने॥३॥
verses.english: On the arrival of the Vidharbha princess accompanied by her son and daughter, king Nala passed his days in great happiness, like the chief of the celestials in the Nandana (garden). The greatly illustrious king, having regained his kingdom and becoming famous among the kings of the Jambudvipa, began once more to rule it.

verses.sanskrit: तथा प्रकाशतां यातो जम्बूद्वीपे स राजसु। पुनः शशासा तद्राज्यं प्रत्याहृत्य महायशाः॥४॥
ईजे च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्विधिवच्चाप्तदक्षिणैः। तथा त्वमपि राजेन्द्र ससुहृद्वक्ष्यसेऽचिरात्॥५॥
verses.english: He duly performed many sacrifices with large Dakshinas to the Brahmanas. O great king, you, too, with your relatives and friends, will soon perform many sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: दुःखमेतादृशं प्राप्तो नलः परपुरञ्जयः। देवनेन नरश्रेष्ठ सभार्यो भरतर्षभ॥६॥
verses.english: foremost of meu, O best of the Bharata race that conqueror of the hostile cities, Nala, thus fell into great distress in consequence of his playing at dice.

verses.sanskrit: एकाकिनैव सुमहन्नलेन पृथिवीपते। दुःखमासादितं घोरं प्राप्तश्चाभ्युदयः पुनः॥७॥
verses.english: O ruler of the earth, Nala alone suffered such great and terrible distress, but he regained his lost glory.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं पुनर्भ्रातृसहितः कृष्णया चैव पाण्डव। रमसेऽस्मिन्महारण्ये धर्ममेवानुचिन्तयन्॥८॥
verses.english: O son of Pandu, you, however, with Krishna (Draupadi) and your brothers, sport here in this great forest, with your heart fixed on virtue.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणैश्च महाभागैर्वेदवेदाङ्गपारगैः। नित्यमन्वास्यसे राजंस्तत्र का परिदेवना॥९॥
verses.english: O king, what cause is there for your sorrow, when you are always mixing with the greatly exalted Brahmanas learned in the Vedas?

verses.sanskrit: कर्कोटकस्य नागस्य दमयन्त्या नलस्य च। ऋतुपर्णस्य राजर्षेः कीर्तनं कलिनाशनम्॥१०॥
verses.english: To recite the history of Naga Karkotaka, of Damayanti, of Nala and of the royal sage Rituparna, is destructive of evil (Kali).

verses.sanskrit: इतिहासमिमं चापि कलिनाशनमच्युत। शक्यमाश्वसितुं श्रुत्वा त्वद्विधेन विशांपते॥११॥
verses.english: O undeteriorating one, O ruler of men, this history, which is destructive of evil (Kali), is capable of comforting persons like you, when they hear it.

verses.sanskrit: अस्थिरत्वं च सञ्चिन्त्य पुरुषार्थस्य नित्यदा। तस्योदये व्यये चापि न चिन्तयितुमर्हसि॥१२॥
verses.english: Considering that human exertion is always futile, you should joy or grieve at prosperity or adversity.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वेतिहासं नृपते समाश्वसिहि मा शुचः। व्यसने त्वं महाराज न विषीदितुमर्हसि॥१३॥
verses.english: O great king, hearing this history, be comforted. Do not grieve. You should not be aggrieved at calamity.

verses.sanskrit: विषमावस्थिते दैवे पौरुषेऽफलतां गते। विषादयन्ति नात्मानं सत्त्वोपाश्रयिणो नराः॥१४॥
verses.english: Reflecting on the caprice of fate and futileness of human exertions, men of selfpossession never allow themselves to be aggrieved.

verses.sanskrit: ये चेदं कथयिष्यन्ति नलस्य चरितं महत्। श्रोष्यन्ति चाप्यभीक्ष्णं वै नालक्ष्मीस्तान्भजिष्यति॥१५॥
verses.english: Those who recite the great history of Nala and those who often hear it are never touched by calamity.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थास्तस्योपपत्स्यन्ते धन्यतां च गमिष्यति। इतिहासमिमं श्रुत्वा पुराणं शश्वदुत्तमम्॥१६॥
verses.english: He, who hears this excellent and old history, gets all his desires fulfilled and obtains wealth and

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रान्पौत्रान्पशूंश्चापि लभते नृषु चाग्र्यताम्। आरोग्यप्रीतिमांश्चैव भविष्यति न संशयः॥१७॥
verses.english: Sons, grandsons, animals, a high position, health and joy. There is no doubt in this.

verses.sanskrit: भयात्त्रास्यसि यच्च त्वमाह्वयिष्यति मां पुनः। अक्षज्ञ इति तत्तेऽहं नाशयिष्यामि पार्थिव॥१८॥
verses.english: O king, the fear, that you entertain that some one would again summon you to play, I shall dispel.

verses.sanskrit: वेदाक्षहृदयं कृत्स्नमहं सत्यपराक्रम। उपपद्यस्व कौन्तेय प्रसन्नोऽहं ब्रवीमि ते॥१९॥
verses.english: O greatly powerful hero, O son of Kunti, I am an expert in the science of dice. I am pleased with you; learn it from me, I shall tell it to you.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततो हृष्टमना राजा बृहदश्वमुवाच ह। भगवन्नक्षहृदयं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥२०॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Thereupon with great joy the king (Yudhishthira) thus spoke to Brihadashva, “O exalted one. I desire to learn the science of dice from you."
verses.bhavadeepa: पुनर्द्यूतं करिष्यसीति राजानं प्रति पूर्वं भीमेसेनेनोक्तं तत्र परिहारमाह वेदेति । वेद वेद्मि । उपपद्यस्व गृहाण ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽक्षहृदयं प्रादात्पाण्डवाय महात्मने। दत्त्वा चाश्वशिरोऽगच्छदुपस्प्रष्टुं महातपाः॥२१॥
verses.english: Thereupon he taught the science to the illustrious son of Pandu. Having taught it, the great ascetic went to Asvasira to bathe.

verses.sanskrit: बृहदश्वे गते पार्थमश्रौषीत्सव्यसाचिनम्। वर्तमनं तपस्युग्रे वायुभक्षं मनीषिणम्॥२२॥
verses.english: When Brihadashva had gone away, he (Yudhishthira) heard that the son of Pritha Savyasachi (Arjuna) was engaged in severe asceticism, living on air. He heard this from the greatly intelligent Brahmanas and ascetics who came to him from various directions and from places of pilgrimage, from mountains and forests. He heard that the mighty Partha (Arjuna) was engaged in such fearful asceticism that none else, before him, had done it.
verses.bhavadeepa: अश्वशिरोऽश्वविद्यां यया बृहदश्व इति मुनेर्नाम । उपस्प्रष्टुं स्नानादिकं कर्तुम् ॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तपस्विभ्यः सम्पतद्भ्यस्ततस्ततः। तीर्थशैलवनेभ्यश्च समेतेभ्यो दृढव्रतः॥२३॥
इति पार्थो महाबाहुर्दुरापं तप आस्थितः। न तथा दृष्टपूर्वोऽन्यः कश्चिदुग्रतपा इति॥२४॥
यथा धनञ्जयः पार्थस्तपस्वी नियतव्रतः। मुनिरेकचरः श्रीमान्धर्मो विग्रहवानिव॥२५॥
verses.english: He heard that Dhananjaya Partha (Arjuna) engaged in asceticism, observing vows of silence and deep in meditation, appeared like the blazing deity, Dharma.

verses.sanskrit: तं श्रुत्वा पाण्डवो राजंस्तप्यमानं महावने। अन्वशोचत कौन्तेयः प्रियं वै भ्रातरं जयम्॥२६॥
verses.english: O king, having heard that his beloved brother, the son of Kunti, Yaja (Arjuna) was thus undergoing asceticism in the great forest Yudhishthira began to grieve.

verses.sanskrit: दह्यमानेन तु हृदा शरणार्थी महावने। ब्राह्मणान्विविधज्ञानान्पर्यपृच्छद्युधिष्ठिरः॥२७॥
verses.english: Thus burning in grief, Yudhishthira sought consolation in the great forest and talked with the Brahmanas learned in all Shastras.
